title: Degenerated current mirror
description: A source-degenerated current mirror: each leg puts a resistor in series with the source. Degeneration does two things. It raises the output resistance by the local-feedback factor $(1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*R_s)$ — the resistor sits in the source, so the source-body generator feeds back through it exactly as $g_m$ does — so the output current holds steadier against the output node voltage. And it improves matching: a threshold mismatch now competes with the IR drop across $R_s$, so its effect on the current divides by $(1 + (g_m + g_{mb})*R_s)$; the threshold generator sits at the gate, so only $g_m$ converts it to a current — but the source lift it causes feeds back through both source-referred generators, so the same $(g_m + g_{mb})$ factor divides it. The price is headroom, the resistor drops $I*R_s$ that the output node must clear on top of the device saturation voltage. Both legs are arranged to drop the same $I_{in}*R_s$ at the target ratio (the K-times output leg uses $R_s/K$), so the two source nodes would sit at one potential if the output leg carried exactly $K*I_{in}$. It does not: the output device sits at a different drain voltage from the diode-connected reference, so it carries a little more or less, and its resistor drops that current times $R_s/K$. So the output device's source is solved, not typed: it is the node at which the device's own current, through $R_s/K$, drops exactly that node voltage. The output device shares the reference's gate wire, so its gate-source voltage is the reference's gate (its diode drop above its own lifted source) less that node, and its source-body bias is the node. That is the degeneration feedback acting on the systematic error itself: a current above target lifts the source, which takes gate-source voltage away and pulls the current back, so the systematic-error equation reads the drain-voltage mismatch divided by roughly the local-feedback factor. The matching-improvement formula is exact only where threshold mismatch dominates; the LUT $g_{ds}$ and Pelgrom spread are the ground truth these equations annotate. Both gates sit on the reference's diode node, so no gate is a port; the output node is held at $V_{out}$, and the supply the reference's ideal source draws from is a port.

params.name: K
params.note: mirror ratio W_out/W_ref; degeneration mirrors are usually 1:1, and the output leg scales its resistor to R_s/K to keep the IR drops matched

params.name: R_s
params.note: reference-leg source-degeneration resistor; the output leg uses R_s/K

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the mirror serves

params.name: k_s
params.note: where the output device's source sits, as a multiple of the reference leg's degeneration drop I_in*R_s. Solved, not set: the output device's current through R_s/K is the source node's voltage, and that node sets the device's gate-source voltage under the shared gate and its body bias. The engine searches for the node at which the two agree; the stored value is never read. It is stated as a multiple of the reference leg's drop so that its range means the same thing whatever the resistor: 1 is that drop, which is where the node sits when the output leg carries exactly K times the input current; it settles a little above or below that where the output leg carries more or less. It is searched between 0, the source at ground, and 2, twice that drop: there the device has less gate-source voltage than the reference while the drop asks for twice its target current, so the node cannot lie beyond it. The V_s equation gives the node in volts

doc.title: Reference (diode) device
doc.description: The diode-connected reference, its source lifted I_in*R_s above ground by the degeneration resistor — the one device on this sheet whose current is typed, so that drop is exact. Its vds is the transistor's own diode drop; its source-body bias is the resistor drop. Exposes its width so the output side sizes as a unit-device multiple, and its gate-source voltage, which with the resistor drop places the gate the two devices share.

params.name: vsb_r
params.note: source above ground by the reference-leg IR drop (body grounded)

equations.name: I_out
equations.note: the output device's current, read off the table at the gate-source voltage, body bias and drain voltage the solved source node gives it

equations.name: sys_err
equations.note: lambda mismatch between the output transistor's drain voltage and the diode point, with the degeneration feedback acting on it: the output leg's own current places its source, so a current above target lifts the source and takes back gate-source voltage. It is the bare drain-voltage mismatch divided by roughly the local-feedback factor

equations.name: R_s_out
equations.note: output-leg resistor; carries K*I_in and drops the same I_in*R_s as the reference leg

equations.name: V_deg
equations.note: the degeneration voltage dropped across the reference leg's resistor, and across the output leg's where it carries exactly K times the input current

equations.name: V_s
equations.note: the output device's source node, in volts: the solved multiple of the reference leg's drop. It is the output device's body bias, the shared gate less it is its gate-source voltage, and the output level less it is its drain-source voltage. With the multiple solved it is the output device's current times R_s_out

equations.name: k_src
equations.note: the output device's own current through the output-leg resistor, as a multiple of the reference leg's drop: where that current puts the source node. k_s is solved to this

equations.name: V_out_min
equations.note: the output compliance floor: the output device's saturation voltage on top of the drop across its resistor (the headroom cost of degeneration). The output device's saturation region holds the output above it

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: output resistance boosted by local series feedback, with the resistor's own series contribution added back. Both source-referred generators feed back through R_s_out, so gmb belongs inside the factor; the trailing R_s_out adds about 1% at these defaults

equations.name: irel_out
equations.note: the OUTPUT device's own inversion level, read back from its operating point

equations.name: sigma_ratio
equations.note: degeneration divides the current spread by the local-feedback factor; estimate, exact only where threshold mismatch dominates
